The candidate version of macOS Tahoe 26.7 released today includes a short video that appears to demonstrate the "visual intelligence" feature on Apple's rumored camera-equipped AirPods in action. Please watch the video below.

macOS 26.7 includes a demo of camera-equipped AirPods

MacRumors discovered a short video included in today's macOS Tahoe 26.7 candidate release, in which a man wearing AirPods appears to ask Siri to remember a book he is looking at. The Siri voiceover says:

The camera itself is not visible in the video, and the earbuds look very similar to the current AirPods Pro. The most noticeable difference is the stem, which appears to be slightly thicker.

Aaron Perris has also posted the same video to X:

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman previously reported that Apple may launch camera-equipped AirPods as early as this year, with the internal codename B790. Earlier today, MacRumors also found references to B790 in the macOS 26.7 candidate release, including code for "visual streaming."

It is worth noting that this AirPods model is reportedly separate from another camera-equipped model Apple has been developing under the codename B798, according to Bloomberg, which is not expected to launch until 2027.

Given Apple's decision to include this demo in the macOS 26.7 candidate release, these camera-equipped AirPods are highly likely to be announced at next month's iPhone event.

What are your thoughts on this video? Let us know in the comments.
